correctness.rationale: The coefficient-normalization error is \(O(n^{-k})\); CRT and a deterministic \(O(Y^{1-k})\) product tail give the joint weak limit. The block-prime lemma gives conditional point probabilities at most 1/min B, with independent uniformly positive good-block probabilities; this proves no atoms. For Hausdorff dimension zero, low-surprisal prefixes occur simultaneously with long prime gaps with positive probability at every scale; their tail-invariant liminf event is probability one by Kolmogorov 0–1. Counting at most \(X^{K+1}\) such prefixes and using interval radii \(O(X^{-(k-1)/\varepsilon})\) gives dimension <=eps(K+1)/(k-1), arbitrarily close to zero. The finite exact tests are consistency only; the infinite assertions rest on the proof.

value.rationale: This determines the limiting global statistical object for natural prime-detecting quasimodular coefficients, and proves the unusually strong combination of atomlessness with concentration on a zero-dimensional Borel set. The full odd-parameter family and the correlated-product dependence are mathematically motivated by its current prime-detection literature; it is not a finite-table re-evaluation or a restatement of the older coefficient formula.
